These products work, not in the allopathic "pharma-medicine" way, but in a terrain-support, consciousness bolstering plant-teacher sort of way.

recABS9cTyYGHFXEG.Body: The Sonic Slider is the flagship tool behind Biofield Tuning itself, a weighted tuning fork hand-tuned to 93.96 Hz, the twelfth harmonic of the Schumann Resonance, Earth's own natural electromagnetic pulse. Its extended handle lets you glide it smoothly across the face, neck, and body, and practitioners and users regularly report support for relaxation, circulation, and nervous system regulation. It's the same fork Chance uses in his own sessions, and a great entry point if you want to bring this work into your own daily routine.
recABS9cTyYGHFXEG.Name: The Sonic Slider

recMVdJjP2VZJyI2m.Body: Clive de Carle has spent decades researching high-quality natural health essentials, from magnesium and fulvic minerals to iodine, selenium, and vegan-sourced vitamin D. His supplements are formulated with a focus on bioavailability, so the body can actually absorb and use what you're taking rather than letting it pass through unused. It's a simple, no-nonsense approach to filling the nutritional gaps most modern diets leave behind.

A biofield tuning practitioner, he uses tuning forks to help clients resolve physical symptoms, break negative patterns, and return to energetic coherence.

recBE7KwrPCyVVZMU.Bio: Gabriel, known on air as Slick Dissident, co-hosts InnerVerse's Vibe Rant show and is a longtime recurring guest on the podcast. He teaches occult symbolism and tarot on his YouTube channel, ranging across the Major Arcana, the esoteric Enneagram, mythology and archetype, mystic linguistics, and the symbolism hidden in popular film. He is best known for Tarot-tories, his own system mapping the 22 Major Arcana and zodiac archetypes onto the geography of the United States.

fields.Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "Your Body Lives Inside Your Mind", "body": "Chance opens by arguing that personality is an idea rather than a reality, and that saying \"that's just how I am\" quietly outsources responsibility for our problems. His one take home sentence is that the body sits inside the mind, not the other way around, and he notes that swapping the M for a W turns mind into wind. In Biofield Tuning's model as he teaches it, cognitive dissonance shows up as stagnant or compartmentalized energy in the field, and that stuck energy tends to surface first as friction in relationships, work and opportunity before it ever shows up in the body."}, {"title": "Reading the Field Like Tree Rings", "body": "Chance walks through his slides of the biofield as a toroidal bioplasma shaped like an apple sliced in half. He describes a double layered boundary that once fooled him into chasing energy that would not clear, and a timeline running from birth at the outer edge to the present at the body, so that halfway through a sixty year old's field corresponds to age thirty. He adds the ancestral river, an Earth star below the feet and a Sun star above the head, and explains that most of his sessions are remote, worked on a table laid out with crystals and candles."}, {"title": "Topher on Plasma, Tides and the Taco", "body": "Topher Gardner, the bodyworker behind BioCharisma, defines plasma as the state between the physical and the metaphysical, and compares it to the tides that cranial sacral practitioners follow, which he says rectify themselves when observed without interference. He recalls living in an ashram with Raja yogis who nicknamed the sudden interruption that arrives just before a breakthrough \"the taco,\" a form of self sabotage he says breeds radical self responsibility. He also maps the zodiacal man onto the legs, with the feet as Pisces, the ankles as Aquarius and the knees as Capricorn."}, {"title": "Procrastinating Ankles and Burned Out Roots", "body": "Working up from the feet, Chance teaches that in his reading the right knee often carries obstacles framed by external authority, the left knee struggles with letting go, and the right ankle holds procrastination and perfectionism, a blend he calls procrastifectionism. He tells how his dog sprained an ankle in holes he had been putting off filling, and argues that perfectionism is an avoidance tactic. At the root, he says the belief that you are only trying hard enough when burned out can keep a body waking early and exhausted, and his advice is not to do the work in your head before it is time."}, {"title": "Gabe on Flow, Wrath and Witnessing", "body": "Gabe keeps notebooks for ideas that come on his walks, because a thought won't survive if it's not born somewhere. When the talk turns to grounding and smell, he notes that wolf reversed is flow and says it feels like we are rewilding ourselves. He reads Athena pulling Achilles back by the hair in the Iliad as the posture of Sagittarius, ties it to the Enneagram's type one, the perfectionist whose shadow is wrath, and calls anger nothing more than a demand for something better. Later he says he wants to get better at being a good witness, and Chance tells him he already is everybody's favorite witness."}]
fields.Intro Paragraph 1: Your body has been speaking a language nobody taught you to read. Every ache, tension, dysfunction, and recurring pattern in your physical form is a coded message from your energy body about the beliefs, emotions, and stories you've been holding onto, often without realizing it. This is the complete map.
fields.Intro Paragraph 2: In this three-hour deep dive with mystical bodyworker Topher Gardner of BioCharisma, we walk the entire biofield anatomy from the ground up: the toroidal structure of your energy field, the double-layered boundary that separates you from the world, the chronological age-rings that store every memory of your life like rings on a tree, the ancestral river that carries inherited patterning forward through generations, and a chakra-by-chakra breakdown of what each region of your body is communicating when something hurts, sticks, or breaks down. By the end you'll have a working language for translating physical symptoms into the underlying beliefs that created them, and a practical sense of how to start reclaiming the parts of your power you've been unconsciously outsourcing.
